newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker ahead of economic data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker ahead of economic data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in moderate trading on Thursday as investors continued to take profits ahead of key economic data due to be released in Canada and the United States on Friday, analysts said.
"The U.S. is flat, so is the (Canada) dollar, and there's a little bit of profit-taking particularly at the long end," said Michael Gregory, economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers in Toronto.
"We've had some decent moves this week with the long end outperforming. Some of that is being given back today," Gregory added.
Canada's benchmark 30-year long bond fell C$0.22 to C$118.27 to yield 6.592 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond lost 2/32 to yield 6.57 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds moved to a spread of two basis points, compared to a spread of one basis point at the close on Wednesday.
Analysts said a soft Canadian dollar failed to offset today's bearish sentiment in the bond market.
Canada's dollar closed slightly weaker on Thursday at C$1.3734 (US$0.7281) after opening the session at C$1.3725 (US$0.7285).
"The (Canada) dollar is a little bit off, so there's a bit more weight on the bonds," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with I.D.E.A. in New York.
Kalirai said the markets were awaiting the release of Friday's key employment data in Canada and producer prices in the United States.
A Reuters survey of economists predicted a jump of 38,800 jobs in employment growth for June, compared to an increase of 61,000 in May.
The same survey forecast Canadian unemployment to dip to 9.4 percent in June from 9.5 percent in May.
A Reuters U.S. survey forecast producer prices would remain unchanged in June from a drop of 0.3 percent in May.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.25 to C$109.17 to yield 6.005 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent, which traded flat to yield 6.25 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 25 basis points from 29 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.09 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.15 percent.
